events.title: Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth Adopts the May 3rd Constitution
events.description: The Great Sejm adopted the Constitution of May 3, 1791, a written national constitution that established a constitutional monarchy, separation of powers among legislative, executive and judicial branches, and expanded rights for townspeople while limiting the power of the magnates.
events.significance: It is regarded as the first modern codified national constitution in Europe and the second in the world after the U.S. Constitution. It remains a symbol of Polish national identity and is commemorated as a national holiday in Poland.

events.title: Birth of Niccolò Machiavelli
events.description: Niccolò Machiavelli was born in Florence, Italy. He became a diplomat, civil servant and political philosopher in the Florentine Republic and later wrote The Prince, a treatise on political power and statecraft.
events.significance: His writings laid foundations for modern political science and realist political theory, and the term 'Machiavellian' entered common language to describe pragmatic and often ruthless political tactics.

events.title: Japan's Postwar Constitution Takes Effect
events.description: The Constitution of Japan, drafted during the Allied occupation and promulgated in November 1946, came into force on May 3, 1947. It established a parliamentary democracy, made the Emperor a symbolic figure, guaranteed fundamental human rights, and included Article 9 renouncing war.
events.significance: The constitution reshaped Japan from an imperial system into a democratic state and has remained unamended since, shaping its pacifist postwar identity. The date is celebrated annually as Constitution Memorial Day.

events.title: Birth of the Modern Cold War Era Milestone: End of the Berlin Blockade Agreement Announced
events.description: On May 4-5, 1949 the Four Powers formally agreed to end the Berlin Blockade, and preparations announced around this time led to the blockade being lifted on May 12, 1949, after the Soviet Union had cut off land access to West Berlin since June 1948.
events.significance: The successful Berlin Airlift and end of the blockade demonstrated Western resolve, accelerated the creation of NATO and the division of Germany into two states, and was a defining early Cold War episode.

events.title: First Unsolicited Mass Commercial Email Sent
events.description: Gary Thuerk, a marketer at Digital Equipment Corporation, sent an unsolicited promotional message about DEC computers to hundreds of users on ARPANET on May 3, 1978.
events.significance: It is widely considered the first spam email, foreshadowing the later growth of unsolicited bulk messaging and the ongoing challenges of email abuse and regulation.
